title: Mitigate microburst-induced batch deadlock causing elevated tail latency
creator: Maya Chen
description:
After multiple customer escalations (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) we observed production incidents where short high-frequency requests (microbursts of small tokens) prevented scheduled flushes in the continuous batching loop. This produced a deadlock-like condition where batches neither filled nor timed_out properly, amplifying queue latency and causing long-context requests to experience extreme tail latency. The issue surfaced after a runtime change that adjusted the batching timer interaction with prefix/KV cache validation.

This ticket tracks investigation, customer mitigations, a fix for the batching loop and the rollout plan across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The goal is to eliminate the deadlock class and restore SLOs for 99.9th percentile latency across affected customers.
steps_to_reproduce: Configure model with long-context (>=16k) and mixed traffic: ~90% tiny (1-3 tokens) microbursts, 10% long-context requests
Enable continuous batching with default timers and KV cache validation enabled
Send microburst traffic at 200rps sustained for 30s followed by a long-context request
Observe that long request waits >10x normal p99 and continuous batches do not flush until connection resets
root_cause_summary: Race between batching flush timer and KV cache validation path introduced in runtime-1.18. Small microburst requests continually reset internal 'fill' heuristics and the timer reschedule logic allowed the batching loop to skip the flush when prefix verification was pending, leading to starvation for long requests which depend on timely KV cache population and preemptive scheduling.
mitigation_applied: Hotfix deployed: 1) force periodic timer wake every 100ms if outstanding requests >0; 2) emergency routing rule to bypass continuous-batcher for flagged customers (fallback to single-request path); and 3) temporary increased priority for long-context requests in the scheduler. Mitigations reduced p99 for impacted customers from 18s to 430ms in canary.

impact_summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported production degradation affecting critical latency SLOs. Incident impacted both hosted API endpoints and Dedicated pools where microburst traffic patterns are common. No data loss or correctness issues observed, primary impact was availability/degraded latency.
